units.title: Call of the night
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: call of the night, between two people whose boilers had both stopped at exactly 02:00: a man asking whether fog counts as weather for the purposes of his gas bill, because his heating was on more. I said I'd raise it with the fog. He thanked me and said I was the first sensible person he'd spoken to all week

units.title: fizzing on the lines in fog
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: For anyone walking the Gilliver back road at night this week and wondering about the crackling overhead: in a fog like this the salt settles on the insulators and they fizz, you can sometimes see a faint blue glow on the old ones. It's mostly harmless and it washes off with the first proper rain. If one starts banging rather than fizzing, ring us.

units.title: Lisle pier in the fog
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: ha, anyway, the pier lights have been on all day at Lisle for three days now because nobody can tell when it's dark... the last ferry came in this evening out of nothing at all, just the horn and then suddenly a whole boat. I've worked that pier six years and it still makes me jump every time.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Thank you, Garvey, that is the salt deposition I keep going on about, described better than I manage. Out of interest, how long does a fizzing insulator usually take to fail, if it ever does? I would guess years rather than weeks, but you'd know better than a retired surveyor with a hand lens.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Years, mostly, Ferrous. Salt makes them track and trip, it doesn't usually break them. What breaks them is old porcelain with a crack you can't see and damp getting in. We've got a few of those about from the seventies. Not saying where. Not saying when.

units.title: Forecourt report
units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: forecourt report: a man bought one egg. just one. paid by card, said thank you, carried it out in both hands like a baby bird. I respect him more than anyone I have met this year.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: was it a good egg. please tell me it was a good egg. I need this for my mental health more than I need the chapter I'm supposed to be writing, which is about protein folding and has nothing to do with eggs, sadly

units.title: New in the catalogue: Gilliver fog signals (1994)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: New in the catalogue this week, given the weather: LB-0301, Gilliver harbour wall in dense fog, November 1994, 31 minutes on DAT. The Carrow Point signal, a ship's horn, the harbour bell, and a man calling for his cat. Provenance complete for once. Comments on the entry welcome as usual.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Producer's note from the overnight show: the doctored image reached our listener line three times before it came down, and each caller added a detail. By the third, the 'evacuation site' had helicopters and a fence. Nobody had seen any of it. That's how this works. Source: my notes, which are dull.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you, my dear, you may call me Maud. I like your line from the novel very much. I shall think of it tonight when I light mine. If you ever come over on the ferry, the house with the blue door by the harbour is mine, and there will be tea, and a lamp.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For the log, since Seth has made it public: one grey heron, bow rail, 07:05, declined to disembark until encouraged with a mop. No damage to the vessel or the heron. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Our gatehouse clock is eleven minutes slow and IT says it is a feature, because the logs are stamped by the server anyway. So I write two times in the book for everything. Nobody has ever asked which one is right.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: this is exactly the right way to post a mystery, thank you. Time, place, what you checked, what you didn't. Please do report back when the forklift driver returns with the keys. Ines
